top_signals.title: Ethereum news (ETH): The $293 million KelpDAO hack shows why DeFi is finally being forced to grow up
top_signals.summary: A $293 million exploit of KelpDAO, linked to a vulnerability in LayerZero’s bridge, highlighted that DeFi’s biggest risks now stem from infrastructure, governance and operational security rather than smart‑contract bugs. Industry leaders such as Lido and Spark say the incident will accelerate a shift toward low‑risk, “boring” DeFi as institutional capital seeks reliability.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The KelpDAO hack spotlights cross‑chain bridge risk, likely compressing valuations for high‑risk DeFi protocols and driving capital toward audited, low‑risk infrastructure while prompting tighter regulatory scrutiny on bridge security.

top_signals.title: SpaceX targets June 11 IPO pricing, picks Nasdaq for historic market debut
top_signals.summary: SpaceX is accelerating its IPO timeline, aiming to price the deal on June 11 and begin trading on Nasdaq around June 12. The company seeks to raise about $75 billion at a $1.75 trillion valuation, making it the largest public offering ever and bringing its sizable Bitcoin treasury into the public markets.
top_signals.why_it_matters: SpaceX’s massive IPO puts a sizable Bitcoin treasury on a public balance sheet, legitimizing crypto as a corporate asset and opening a new liquidity source that could attract more institutional capital to the broader crypto ecosystem.

top_signals.title: The man who built Saudi Arabia’s digital payment rails has a bold 2030 plan to bring trillions onchain
top_signals.summary: Faisal Monai, the architect of Saudi Arabia’s digital payments system, is spearheading a $12.5 billion initiative through droppRWA to tokenize real‑world assets, beginning with real estate. He envisions a sovereign‑grade, stablecoin‑based tokenized financial infrastructure nationwide by 2030, with real‑estate settlement live by late 2026, positioning Saudi Arabia as a model for other G20 economies.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Saudi Arabia’s $12.5 billion tokenization drive creates a sovereign‑backed stablecoin and RWA pipeline, establishing a regulatory blueprint that could unlock trillions of on‑chain assets and position early‑stage tokenization platforms for rapid scaling.

top_signals.title: Hana Bank agrees to buy $670 million stake in Upbit operator Dunamu
top_signals.summary: Hana Bank will purchase a 6.55% stake in Dunamu, the operator of South Korea’s Upbit exchange, for roughly 1 trillion won ($670 million). The investment positions Hana as Dunamu’s fourth‑largest shareholder and includes joint development of a won‑pegged stablecoin, blockchain remittances and tokenized securities, coinciding with new Korean digital‑asset regulations.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Hana Bank’s $670 million stake in Dunamu and joint stablecoin and tokenized‑security projects validate the Korean market, accelerate infrastructure development and create co‑investment opportunities for Web3 startups seeking regulated entry points.

top_signals.title: AI miner IREN raises $3 billion to accelerate AI cloud and data center buildout
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin miner IREN raised approximately $3 billion through a convertible senior notes offering to fund its transition into AI cloud and hyperscale data‑center infrastructure. The financing, which grew from an initial $2 billion target, will back GPU purchases from Nvidia and Dell and other AI‑related capex, while the company's shares slipped about 3% in pre‑market trading.
top_signals.why_it_matters: IREN’s $3 billion financing to build AI‑focused data centers merges mining scale with hyperscale compute, potentially lowering cloud costs for blockchain workloads and attracting cross‑industry investors to high‑performance Web3 infrastructure.

top_signals.title: Here is why Wall Street is racing to tokenize the entire stock market
top_signals.summary: Wall Street firms are accelerating efforts to tokenize equities, highlighted by Bullish’s $4.2 billion acquisition of transfer agent Equiniti to enable on‑chain issuance and record‑keeping. Proponents argue tokenized securities could deliver 24/7 trading, near‑instant settlement, and richer ownership data, though regulatory and market‑structure challenges remain.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Bullish’s acquisition of Equiniti to enable on‑chain equity issuance brings deep liquidity and regulatory expertise to tokenized securities, raising the competitive bar for early‑stage tokenization platforms.

worth_a_read.note: Institutional Shift Toward “Boring” Low‑Risk DeFi The $293 million KelpDAO hack and the $10.8 million Thorchain exploit have sharpened investors’ focus on infrastructure, governance and operational security rather than pure smart‑contract risk. Lido and Spark warned that institutional capital will now favor protocols with audited bridges, modest yields and transparent governance. Expect a migration of new capital into “boring” DeFi products such as custodial lending, on‑chain money‑market funds and audited bridge solutions.

Tokenization Liquidity Networks Gaining Critical Mass BlackRock and Janus Henderson secured a $1 billion daily stablecoin liquidity line from Basin, while Animoca‑backed NUVA is onboarding $19 billion of real‑world assets onto Ethereum. JPMorgan’s SEC filing for a tokenized Treasury money‑market fund adds another major custodian to the mix. The emerging pattern points to a layered liquidity stack that will enable instant redemptions and 24/7 trading of tokenized securities, accelerating institutional adoption of on‑chain asset classes.

Circle’s Expansion Beyond USDC with the Arc Blockchain Circle raised $222 million in a presale that values its new Arc layer‑1 at $3 billion, positioning the network as an institution‑focused rail for stablecoins and tokenized assets. The funding round attracted a16z crypto, BlackRock and ARK Invest, signaling confidence that Circle can compete in the broader blockchain infrastructure space. Arc is likely to become a preferred settlement layer for regulated stablecoin issuers and tokenized fund managers seeking compliance‑ready throughput.

U.S. Legislative Momentum Provides Stablecoin Clarity The Senate Banking Committee advanced the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act to the full Senate floor with a bipartisan 15‑9 vote, creating a clear regulatory framework for dollar‑stablecoins and tokenized securities. The bill’s passage will reduce legal uncertainty for issuers and could prompt European regulators to align MiCA provisions with U.S. standards. Anticipate a surge in stablecoin issuance and cross‑border tokenized fund structures as firms position for a harmonized global regime.

Traditional Finance Deepening Direct Crypto Exposure Hana Bank’s $670 million purchase of a 6.55 % stake in Dunamu, KDDI’s $65 million acquisition of a 14.9 % share in Coincheck, and SpaceX’s planned $75 billion IPO that will bring a sizable Bitcoin treasury to public markets illustrate a rapid convergence of legacy finance and crypto. These moves provide established distribution channels for stablecoins, tokenized assets and on‑chain payments, and they signal that large banks and telecoms see crypto as a core component of future financial services. Expect accelerated rollout of won‑pegged stablecoins, blockchain remittance products and tokenized securities in Asia and beyond.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, This week the crypto landscape showed both growing pains and bold expansion. The $293 million KelpDAO exploit, traced to a vulnerability in LayerZero’s bridge, reminded us that the biggest risks in DeFi now sit in infrastructure, governance and operational security rather than pure code bugs. Leaders across the sector are already talking about a shift toward low‑risk, “boring” DeFi products as institutional capital demands reliability. Across the broader market, SpaceX is accelerating its historic IPO, targeting a June 11 pricing and a Nasdaq debut the following day. The company aims to raise roughly $75 billion at a $1.75 trillion valuation, bringing a sizable Bitcoin treasury into the public arena and setting a new benchmark for crypto‑enabled corporate finance. In the Middle East, the architect of Saudi Arabia’s digital payment rails unveiled a $12.5 billion tokenisation plan that will start with real‑estate assets. By 2030 the kingdom hopes to run a sovereign‑grade, stablecoin‑based financial infrastructure, with the first real‑estate settlement expected by late 2026. The ambition positions Saudi Arabia as a potential model for other G20 economies. Asia saw a strategic partnership as Hana Bank agreed to purchase a $670 million stake in Dunamu, the operator of South Korea’s Upbit exchange. The deal makes Hana the fourth‑largest shareholder and opens a joint effort on a won‑pegged stablecoin, blockchain remittances and tokenised securities, aligning with the country’s new digital‑asset regulations. Finally, AI miner IREN closed a $3 billion convertible notes offering to fund its pivot into AI cloud and hyperscale data‑centres. The capital will underwrite GPU purchases from Nvidia and Dell, accelerating the convergence of crypto mining and AI workloads. On the metrics side, total stablecoin supply rose to $165.3 billion, up 1.8 percent, while Bitcoin ETF inflows hit $1.5 billion, a 12 percent weekly gain. Ethereum daily active addresses climbed 3.2 percent to 1.15 million, indicating sustained user interest even as DeFi TVL slipped slightly. What themes will dominate the next week and how will they shape capital allocation in Europe’s crypto ecosystem? #Web3 #Crypto #Blockchain #CryptoVC #WeeklyDigest
